about.title: A house for Indian art, and the hands that make it
about.intro: We work directly with artists and craft partners across India. The maker stays visible, and the story stays with the work.
about.lede: SnehaVrinda Kala began as a home for art in all its forms — not a marketplace for objects, but a place where a tradition and the person carrying it stay attached to the work.
about.p1: Every listing shows who made the piece, what it is made from, how to care for it, and whether it is ready to ship or made to order. Nothing is presented as anonymous. If you cannot name the maker, you cannot really know the work.
about.p2: Custom commissions follow a deliberate process — brief, quote, proofs, approval, delivery — so you know exactly what to expect before a brush touches paper.
about.p3: We believe in fair partner terms, transparent attribution, and craft you can trust. The maker stays visible, and the story stays with the work.
about.principlesTitle: Four things we will not compromise

p1.title: The maker is named
p1.body: Every work carries its artist. Attribution is not a marketing line; it is the difference between art and inventory.

p2.title: Handmade, or it is not here
p2.body: We do not sell prints presented as originals, and we do not stock imported goods dressed as craft.

p3.title: Fair terms, stated plainly
p3.body: Artists are paid on agreed terms with milestones, and commissions are quoted before any work begins.

p4.title: Nothing is rushed
p4.body: Some pieces take weeks. Natural pigment, handloom cloth and made-to-order work have their own pace, and we keep it.

about.behindTitle: What happens before you see it
about.behindAlt: A work in progress in the studio

s1.d: Cloth is stiffened with tamarind seed and chalk, or paper is sized, or the panel is primed. Nothing is painted on an unprepared surface.

s2.d: In most of these traditions the drawing is a single unbroken discipline. The border is often drawn last but planned first.

s3.d: Natural pigment, often made in the studio. Shading is rare; a form is read by its outline and its fill.

s4.t: It is signed, and it is explained
s4.d: The maker's name, and usually a note of what the symbols mean. That note is what travels with the work.

faq.title: Questions, answered
faq.intro: Everything buyers ask before ordering — shipping, customs, returns, commissions and how payment works. If your question is not here, write to us and a person will answer.
faq.stillNeedBody: There is no support bot here. Write to the address below and the reply comes from the studio in Bikaner.

buying.heading: Buying
buying.a1: Yes. Each work is painted, woven or shaped by hand, and is a single piece. What you see photographed is the work you receive. Because of that, no two pieces are identical even within the same art form.
buying.q2: Why is a piece I saw earlier no longer listed?
buying.a2: Originals sell once. When a work is sold it comes off the shop, and we do not offer reproductions of it. If you were looking at something specific, write to us and we will tell you whether something similar is in progress.
buying.q3: Can you make something to my size or palette?
buying.a3: Often, yes. Commissions start from size, subject and the tradition you have in mind. Begin with the commission request form and you will get a quote with a timeline before any payment.
buying.q4: Which currencies can I pay in?
buying.a4: Prices are shown in INR, USD, GBP, EUR and AED. Switching the currency in the header converts the catalogue at a rate we keep current; the amount charged is the one shown at checkout.

shipping.heading: Shipping & customs
shipping.a1: Across India, and to the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, the European Union and the Gulf. Choose your country at checkout and we quote the courier for that destination.
shipping.a2: Ready-to-ship works leave Bikaner within 2–3 working days. Made-to-order pieces show their production time on the product page. International orders usually add 5–12 days in transit depending on the destination.
shipping.a3: Orders leaving India may attract import duty or local tax charged by your customs authority on delivery. That is not included in the price you pay us, and we cannot estimate it reliably for every country. If you need certainty before ordering, write to us and we will tell you what we know for your destination.
shipping.a4: Works are packed in material-specific housing — rigid board and corner protection for canvases, padded rolls for textiles, foam cradles for ceramics and metalwork. Fragile pieces are insured in transit.

returns.heading: Returns & care
returns.a1: If a work arrives damaged or is not what you ordered, tell us within 48 hours of delivery with photographs and we will arrange a replacement or refund. Change-of-mind returns are accepted within 7 days for ready-to-ship pieces, provided the work is returned in its original packing. Commissions are made for you and cannot be returned.
returns.q2: What if a delivery arrives damaged?
returns.a2: Photograph the packaging and the work before moving it, then write to us the same day. Keep the packaging until the claim is settled — the courier will usually need to inspect it.
returns.q3: How do I care for the work?
returns.a3: Keep paintings and textiles out of direct sunlight and away from damp walls. Do not wipe painted surfaces; dust with a dry, soft brush. Metalwork such as bidriware should not be scrubbed — a dry cloth is enough. Each order ships with a care note for its material.

payments.heading: Payments & security
payments.q1: Which payment methods do you accept?
payments.a1: Cards (Visa, Mastercard, RuPay), UPI including Google Pay and Paytm, and net banking. Payments are processed by Razorpay; card details are entered on their secure page and never touch our servers.
payments.q2: Do you store my card details?
payments.a2: No. We never see or store card numbers. The payment processor handles the transaction and returns only a confirmation to us.
payments.a3: The charge appears under our registered business name alongside the payment processor. If you do not recognise a charge, write to us with the date and amount and we will trace it.

disclaimer.title: Disclaimer
disclaimer.intro: What we claim about the work, and what we do not. Written to be read before you order rather than discovered afterwards.

variation.heading: Handmade means variation
variation.p1: Every work here is made by hand, one at a time. Brushwork, weave density, glaze pooling, metal patina and the depth of a pigment all vary between pieces, and often within a single piece. That variation is the point of the craft, not a fault in it.
variation.p2: Photographs are taken under studio light and colour-corrected to represent the work as accurately as we can. Screens differ, though: the same madder red can read warm on one display and cool on another. If an exact shade matters to you, ask before ordering and we will send additional photographs in daylight.

aging.heading: Natural materials age
aging.p1: Natural pigments, cotton and silk cloth, wood, brass and silver change over time. Indigo may soften, brass will darken, silver will tarnish. This is expected and is described in the care note sent with each order.
aging.p2: We describe materials as accurately as we can from what the maker used. Where a work incorporates a material we cannot verify — reclaimed wood, for instance, or a pigment a family has mixed for generations — we say so rather than assert a provenance we cannot prove.

authenticity.heading: Authenticity we can stand behind
authenticity.p1: Each work is accompanied by a signed certificate naming the artist and the tradition. That is a statement about who made the piece and under which practice, and it is one we can substantiate.
authenticity.p2: It is not an appraisal. Nothing on this site is a valuation, an investment opinion, or a promise that a piece will hold or gain value. Art is bought because it is worth living with, not because a shop forecast its price.

pricing.heading: Prices, currency and duties
pricing.p1: Prices are set in Indian rupees. Amounts shown in other currencies are converted from INR at a rate we keep current and rounded for clarity; the amount charged is the one displayed at checkout.
pricing.p2: Orders leaving India may attract import duty, VAT or a handling fee levied by the destination country's customs authority. Those charges are the buyer's responsibility and are not included in the price paid to us. We cannot calculate them reliably for every destination and will not pretend otherwise.

payment.heading: Payment processing
payment.p1: Card, UPI and net-banking payments are processed by a third party. We do not receive or store your card number, CVV or UPI PIN. The processor confirms only that a payment succeeded.
payment.p2: For that reason, disputes about a charge are resolved with the processor and your bank as well as with us. If you do not recognise a charge from us, write to hello@snehavrinda.in with the date and amount and we will trace it.

culture.heading: Cultural reference and language
culture.p1: The glossary and journal describe traditions, terms and histories as part of a living practice. Regional names vary — the same motif can carry different words in different states — and we name the variant we mean where it matters.
culture.p2: Where we describe a tradition's history, we rely on published sources and on the makers themselves. If you believe something here misstates a practice, tell us. Corrections from practitioners take precedence over our wording.

links.heading: Links and third parties
links.p1: Some pages link to external sites, such as a courier's tracking page or an artisan collective. We do not control those sites and are not responsible for their content or their handling of your data.
links.p2: Social profiles linked from this site are official accounts of the studio. We do not run, endorse or moderate other accounts using our name.

limitation.heading: Limitation
limitation.p1: Nothing here excludes liability that cannot lawfully be excluded, including for death or personal injury caused by negligence, or for fraud. Beyond that, our liability for any order is limited to the amount you paid for that order.
limitation.p2: This page is written in plain language for clarity. It is not legal advice, and the terms of sale at checkout govern where the two differ.

authenticity.title: What you are actually buying
authenticity.intro: A handmade work asks you to trust a photograph. Here is exactly what stands behind it, and what happens if it is ever wrong.

a1.title: One pair of hands
a1.body: Every work on this site is made by the artist named on it. Nothing is resold from a wholesale catalogue, and nothing is machine-printed and called handmade. If a piece took a month, the making time is stated on the product page before you buy.

a2.title: Signed and dated
a2.body: Paintings and drawings arrive signed. Textile and craft pieces carry a maker's label sewn or stamped on. The signature is not a decoration — it is what lets a piece be identified later, and it is the first thing to look at if you ever resell or insure it.

a3.title: Photographed before packing
a3.body: Each piece is photographed as finished, from more than one angle, before it is wrapped. Those photographs are the record we send you, and they are the reference we use ourselves if there is ever a question about condition.

a4.title: A written record
a4.body: Your parcel includes a card stating the work's title, the artist, the materials, the art form and the date it was completed. It is written for the drawer, not the website — the thing you keep when the packaging is gone.

a5.title: Natural variation is the point
a5.body: Handmade work is not uniform. Dye lots differ, a brush line is not a printed edge, handloom cloth has slubs. We describe material and finish on each listing, and variation within that description is a sign the piece was made by a person.

a6.title: If it is not right, it goes back
a6.body: If a piece arrives damaged, or materially different from its description and photographs, we make it right: replacement where the work can be repeated, refund where it cannot. See the returns policy for how to start that.

willNot.w1: We will not sell a print and call it an original painting.
willNot.w2: We will not put another maker's name on a piece to sell it faster.
willNot.w3: We will not use a stock photograph in place of the actual work you will receive, except where a piece is made to order and the listing says so.

authenticity.mailPre: If you ever believe a piece was misdescribed, write to
authenticity.mailPost: with the order reference. We would rather take a piece back than have someone own something they were misled about.

customArt.title: Let's create something together
customArt.intro: Not everything should be bought off a wall. Tell an artist what you have in mind — a portrait, a mural, a textile for a particular room — and they will tell you honestly what is possible.
customArt.whatTitle: The work comes after the conversation

s1.title: Share your idea
s1.body: A sentence is enough to begin. Tell us what you have in mind, and attach a reference if you have one — a photograph, a room, a colour.

s2.title: Tell us the story
s2.body: Who is it for? Is it a wedding, a memory, a room that needs something? The story is what the artist actually works from.

s3.title: We discuss your vision
s3.body: An artist considers feasibility, rights, schedule and availability — and says plainly if it cannot be done, and why.

s4.title: Receive a real quote
s4.body: Scope, deliverables, timeline, revision allowance, deposit and expiry, all in writing. Nothing is hidden in a range.

s5.title: The creation begins
s5.body: Accept the quote and pay the deposit. Work starts after that, and you get proofs at each stage.

s6.title: Your artwork becomes real
s6.body: Approve the final proof, and the finished work is packed and sent to you with its maker's name on it.

learn.title: Learn
learn.intro: What the words mean, what the work is made of, and where the traditions come from. No shop on this page — only what a visitor needs in order to see.
learn.wordsIntro: Sixteen terms, most of them untranslated on shop pages that use them constantly. Each is given in its own language, because the English word is usually a lossy translation.
learn.materialsTitle: What the work is made of
learn.materialsIntro: Every material here is chosen for a reason that can be stated. A tradition that used rice paste did so because a household already had rice — not because rice is picturesque.
learn.historyIntro: Nine moments, in ranges rather than single years — because the dates are argued about, and pretending otherwise would be a lie told in the service of tidiness.
learn.journalLink: The journal — essays on technique and history →

home.lede: Every piece here was made by a hand that learned the form from someone. We work with makers who have inherited their tradition and are passing it on.
home.machineCan: A machine can repeat a shape a million times.
home.machineCannot: What it cannot do is decide, on a Tuesday afternoon, that the border needs one more fish — and then paint it.
home.craftNote: Every work here was made by one person, in one place, over time that no one was billing for. We keep the maker visible because that is the entire difference between an artwork and a product.
home.kolam: Drawn at the door before sunrise, a kolam welcomes whoever arrives. Consider this one drawn for you.
home.artFormsIntro: Madhubani, Warli, Pattachitra, Gond and Kalamkari — original paintings and handmade pieces, each with its maker named.
home.artistBody: Madhubani is painted with a nib, a twig and a fingertip. A single panel can take a month, and the border is often planned before the centre.
home.artistBody2: We work with makers who have inherited their form and are teaching it on. Every work here carries the name of the person who made it.
home.customBody: Have an idea? Let's create it together — portraits, paintings, décor, or something that does not exist yet.
home.artOfIndiaBody: Every tradition here began with a maker, a material and a reason. We work with artists across India to keep those reasons visible.
home.processBody: Not a checkout. A conversation, a quote, a proof, and then the weeks it actually takes.

policies.shippingIntro: We ship across India through our fulfilment partner. Dispatch timelines depend on the product type:
policies.shippingReadyBody: dispatched within 2–3 business days of order confirmation.
policies.shippingMadeBody: production lead time is shown on each product page before you order.
policies.shippingCustomBody: timeline is agreed in the quote and tracked through milestones.
policies.shippingOutro: Tracking details are shared once the shipment is created. Fragile and oversized items use material-specific packaging and may require special handling.
policies.returnsIntro: Return conditions vary by product type because some work is made especially for you:
policies.returnsReadyBody: eligible for return within 7 days of delivery if unused and in original condition.
policies.returnsMadeBody: not eligible for return unless damaged, incorrect, or not as described, since it is produced for your order.
policies.returnsCustomBody: governed by the milestone agreement in your quote. Deposits are non-refundable once work begins unless the artist is unable to proceed.
policies.returnsDamagedBody: contact us with photos within 48 hours of delivery for a replacement or refund.

policies.privacyP1: We collect only the information needed to process your order, deliver your purchase, and manage custom commissions. This includes contact details, delivery address, payment references, and any reference files you upload for a commission.
policies.privacyP2: Your reference uploads are stored privately, served only through short-lived authorized access, and retained per our retention policy. We do not sell your personal data.
policies.privacyP3: Marketing emails are sent only with your separate consent, and you can opt out at any time. Transactional messages (order updates, shipment tracking, commission progress) are part of the service and are not marketing.
policies.privacyP4: For access, correction, or deletion requests, contact us at hello@snehavrinda.in.
policies.termsP1: Welcome to SnehaVrinda Kala. By placing an order or submitting a custom request, you agree to these terms, our shipping policy, and our returns & refunds policy.
policies.termsP2: All artwork and product images are licensed from the artist for display and sale. Reproduction or commercial reuse requires the artist’s permission.
policies.termsP3: Prices are in Indian Rupees (₹) and include applicable taxes as shown at checkout. Orders are confirmed only after payment is verified server-side.
policies.termsP4: Disputes or grievances can be raised through our contact channel. We aim to acknowledge grievances promptly and resolve them within the published timeline.
